To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the dc voltage control is a key factor in the electromechanical stability of a power system with VSC-HVAC link; 2) the power control has a negligible effect on electromechanical oscillation modes; 3) the dc power flow controller has a negligible effect in both electromechanical oscillations and dc system dynamics; and 4) the power controller has a significant impact on dc dynamics.
the VSC-HVdc control strategies can have a significant effect on the ac system electromechanical dynamics, but the effect is not as strong as that of the ac network itself.
the VSC-HVdc power controller can have significant effects on the electromechanical stability of the ac network.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the VSC-HV DC power controller has the potential to improve the electromechanical stability of the ac network, especially when the VSC-HVD C link is located in a weak area of the network.
the dc system dynamics and ac system electromechanical oscillations are closely coupled and should be considered together in the design and operation of VSC-Hvdc.
